Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 1) The maternity cycle starts from:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The maternity cycle starts from fertilization. It continues through pregnancy, labour and puerperium. It extends up to the period before next conception.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 2) The correct sequence of maternity cycle is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The stages are fertilization, antenatal/prenatal period, intranatal period, postnatal period and inter-conceptional period. This sequence follows the natural reproductive cycle. Inter-conceptional period comes after postnatal period.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 3) The antenatal period refers to:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Antenatal or prenatal period is the period of pregnancy before birth. It is the time for ANC visits, screening and prevention. Intranatal period refers to labour and delivery.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 4) The intranatal period means:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Intranatal period is the period of labour and delivery. Antenatal comes before it. Postnatal period follows delivery.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 5) The previous WHO minimum ANC visit schedule recommends:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The previous WHO minimum ANC schedule included 4 visits. The visits were distributed from early pregnancy to term. The uploaded file also mentions updated 8 contacts.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 6) Updated WHO 2016 ANC contact schedule recommends:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: WHO 2016 updated schedule recommends 8 contacts. They occur approximately at 12, 20, 26, 30, 34, 36, 38 and 40 weeks. This is different from the old 4-visit schedule.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 7) The ideal number of ANC visits mentioned is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The ideal ANC visit as 14. Minimum old schedule was 4 visits. Updated WHO contact schedule is 8 contacts.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 8) The first ANC visit in the previous WHO minimum schedule should be before:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The first ANC visit should be before 12 weeks. Early registration allows early risk detection. It also helps plan screening and supplementation.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 9) In the previous WHO minimum ANC schedule, the second visit is between:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The second visit is scheduled between 14–26 weeks. The first visit is before 12 weeks. The third visit is between 28–34 weeks.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 10) The third ANC visit in previous WHO minimum schedule is between:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The third ANC visit is between 28–34 weeks. This period is important for fetal growth and maternal complications. The fourth visit is near term.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 11) The fourth ANC visit in previous WHO minimum schedule is at:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The fourth ANC visit is between 36–38 weeks or at term. It helps assess readiness for delivery. Birth preparedness and danger signs are reinforced.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 12) The first contact in updated WHO 2016 ANC schedule is approximately at:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: WHO 2016 schedule starts around 12 weeks. Later contacts occur at 20, 26, 30, 34, 36, 38 and 40 weeks. This gives more frequent contact than the old schedule.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 13) Which is included in routine history and examination during ANC?
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: ANC examination includes weight, blood pressure and height. Abdominal examination is also done. Fundal height, fetal movements and fetal heart sound are assessed.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 14) Abdominal examination during ANC includes fundal height, fetal movement and:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: ANC abdominal examination includes fundal height, fetal movements and fetal heart sound. These help assess fetal growth and well-being. They are part of routine antenatal examination.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 15) The most important test in ANC mentioned in the file is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.option2: ABO blood grouping and Rh typing
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: ABO blood grouping and Rh typing are mentioned as the most important test. They are important for pregnancy planning and transfusion safety. Rh status is especially important for Rh incompatibility prevention.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 16) Hb level in ANC is mainly done for screening of:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Hemoglobin level is checked to screen for anemia. Anemia is an important maternal risk factor. Detection allows iron-folic acid correction and follow-up.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 17) Blood sugar during ANC is mainly done for screening of:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Blood sugar is done for GDM screening. GDM can affect both mother and fetus. Early detection helps dietary and medical management.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 18) Urine test in ANC is mainly done for:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Urine test detects proteinuria and UTI. Proteinuria may suggest pre-eclampsia. UTI detection is important because pregnancy increases risk of urinary infection.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 19) HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B screening are included under:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: ANC screening includes HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B testing. These infections may affect mother and fetus. Detection allows timely treatment and prevention of transmission.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 20) Iron-folic acid supplementation during ANC is mainly for prevention of:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Iron-folic acid is an important antenatal supplement. Iron helps prevent anemia. Folic acid is important for fetal development and prevention of deficiency-related problems.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 21) Deworming with albendazole in pregnancy is given:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The file mentions deworming with albendazole after the second trimester. It is part of supplementation and prevention. Timing is important in pregnancy.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 22) TT vaccination in ANC is mainly for prevention of:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: TT vaccination protects against tetanus. It is important for both mother and newborn. It is a routine preventive component of antenatal care.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 23) Counseling during ANC includes nutrition, danger signs and:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: ANC counseling includes nutrition and danger signs. It also includes birth preparedness, postnatal care and breastfeeding initiation. Counseling helps reduce avoidable delay.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 24) Counseling about breastfeeding initiation is included in:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Breastfeeding initiation is discussed during ANC counseling. The mother should be prepared before delivery. It improves early newborn feeding practice.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 25) Swelling of feet during pregnancy is listed as:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Swelling of feet is included among danger signs in pregnancy. It may indicate hypertensive disorder or other complications. It should not be ignored.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 26) Fits during pregnancy is a danger sign suggestive of:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Fits are listed as a danger sign in pregnancy. They may suggest eclampsia in the proper clinical context. Urgent evaluation is needed.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 27) Headache and blurring of vision in pregnancy may suggest:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Headache and blurring of vision are danger signs in pregnancy. They may occur with pre-eclampsia/eclampsia. They require urgent attention.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 28) Bleeding per vagina during pregnancy is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Bleeding or discharge per vagina is listed as a danger sign. It may indicate serious obstetric complications. Prompt assessment is needed.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 29) Infancy is defined as:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Infancy extends from birth to 1 year. Neonate is only the first 28 days. Post-neonatal period extends from 28th day to 1 year.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 30) Neonatal period is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Neonate means first 28 days of life. This period has high vulnerability. Neonatal mortality is calculated within this period.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 31) Post-neonatal period is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Post-neonatal period extends from 28th day to 1 year. It is part of infancy. Neonatal period comes before it.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 32) Pre-school age group is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Pre-school age is 1–4 years. School age is 5–14 years. Infancy is birth to 1 year.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 33) School age group is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: School age is 5–14 years. This is different from pre-school age. Pre-school age is 1–4 years.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 34) TORCH infections are important because they can:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.option2: Cross placenta and cause congenital infection
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: TORCH refers to infections that can cross the placenta. They can cause congenital infection in the fetus. They are important in maternal and child health.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 35) In TORCH, T stands for:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: T in TORCH stands for toxoplasmosis. It is caused by Toxoplasma gondii. It can produce congenital infection.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 36) In TORCH, R stands for:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: R in TORCH stands for rubella. Rubella infection in pregnancy can affect the fetus. It is a classical congenital infection.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 37) In TORCH, C stands for:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: C in TORCH stands for cytomegalovirus. CMV is an important congenital infection. It may cross the placenta and affect the fetus.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 38) “Other infections” in TORCH include:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.option1: Syphilis, varicella-zoster, parvovirus B19, HIV, hepatitis B and C
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.option2: Cholera, typhoid and bacillary dysentery only
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The O in TORCH includes several other congenital infections. The file lists syphilis, varicella-zoster, parvovirus B19, HIV and hepatitis B/C. These can affect pregnancy outcome.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 39) NMR is defined as deaths of newborns during first 28 days per:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Neonatal mortality rate is deaths of newborns during first 28 days per 1,000 live births. It reflects newborn survival. Low birth weight is mentioned as the most common cause in the file.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 40) The current Bangladesh NMR status mentioned is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Current NMR as 17 per 1,000 live births. The SDG target is below 12 per 1,000. Low birth weight is listed as the most common cause.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 41) The SDG target for NMR is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The SDG target for NMR is below 12 per 1,000 live births. current Bangladesh NMR as 17 per 1,000. NMR focuses on first 28 days of life.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 42) Most common cause of NMR mentioned is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Low birth weight is mentioned as the most common cause of NMR. NMR measures death in first 28 days. Reducing LBW improves neonatal survival.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 43) IMR is deaths of infants under 1 year per:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: IMR is deaths of infants under 1 year per 1,000 live births in a year. It is a key child health indicator. It reflects living standard and MCH service effectiveness.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 44) The current Bangladesh IMR status mentioned is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Current IMR as 24 per 1,000 live births. The SDG target is below 12 per 1,000. Diarrhoea is listed as the most common cause.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 45) IMR is regarded as the most important universal indicator of:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: IMR is regarded as the most important universal indicator of health status of a community. It also reflects level of living. It indicates effectiveness of MCH services.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 46) Most common cause of IMR mentioned is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Diarrhoea is listed as the most common cause of IMR . IMR covers death under 1 year. It includes both neonatal and post-neonatal deaths.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 47) MMR is expressed as maternal deaths per:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Maternal mortality ratio is maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. It reflects maternal health service quality. It is an important reproductive health indicator.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 48) The current Bangladesh MMR status is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Current MMR as 173 per 100,000 live births. The SDG target is below 70 per 100,000. Hemorrhage is listed as the most common cause.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 49) The SDG target for MMR is below:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: SDG target for MMR is below 70 per 100,000 live births. Bangladesh MMR as 173 per 100,000. Maternal death reduction is a major global target.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 50) Most common cause of MMR :
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Hemorrhage is mentioned as the most common cause of MMR. Due to APH and PPH. Prevention and rapid management are essential.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 51) Elderly primigravida is defined in the file as primigravida above:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Elderly primigravida is listed as age more than 30 years. It is a high-risk pregnancy factor. Such mothers need careful antenatal monitoring.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 52) Short-statured primigravida is defined as height:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Short-statured primigravida means 140 cm and below. It is listed as a high-risk mother feature. Short stature may be associated with obstetric difficulty.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 53) Which of the following is a high-risk pregnancy condition?
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Malpresentation is listed as a high-risk condition. Other examples include APH, pre-eclampsia, eclampsia and anemia. High-risk mothers need closer supervision.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 54) Prolonged pregnancy is defined in the file as:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.option1: 7 days after expected date of delivery
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.option2: 10 days after expected date of delivery
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.option3: 14 days after expected date of delivery
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.option4: 21 days after expected date of delivery
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Prolonged pregnancy is listed as 14 days after expected date of delivery. It is included under high-risk mother. It needs proper assessment and management.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 55) Three or more consecutive spontaneous abortions indicate:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Three or more consecutive spontaneous abortions are listed as high-risk. Previous bad obstetric history increases future pregnancy risk. Such mothers need careful antenatal care.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 56) Previous caesarean section or instrumental delivery is:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Previous caesarean or instrumental delivery is listed as a high-risk factor. It may affect delivery planning. History of previous stillbirth or intrauterine death is also high-risk.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 57) Low birth weight is defined as birth weight less than:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Low birth weight means birth weight less than 2500 g, irrespective of gestational age. It may be due to prematurity, intrauterine growth restriction or both. LBW babies have higher risk of morbidity and mortality. This is why antenatal nutrition, anemia control and fetal growth monitoring are important.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 58) Perinatal mortality usually includes late fetal deaths and early neonatal deaths up to:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Perinatal mortality combines stillbirths/late fetal deaths with early neonatal deaths. Early neonatal death usually means death within first 7 completed days of life. It reflects quality of antenatal, intranatal and immediate newborn care. It is useful for assessing obstetric and neonatal services together.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 59) Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: Exclusive breastfeeding means only breast milk, with no other food or drink except necessary medicines. It is recommended for the first 6 months of life. It reduces diarrhoeal illness and improves infant nutrition. After 6 months, appropriate complementary feeding should start while breastfeeding continues.

Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.question: 60) The “three delays” model in maternal mortality includes delay in deciding to seek care, delay in reaching care and delay in:
Maternal & Child Health, ANC, High risk.exp: The three delays are delay in deciding to seek care, delay in reaching a health facility and delay in receiving adequate care. This model explains preventable maternal deaths. It is closely linked with birth preparedness, emergency transport and quality obstetric care. ANC counseling helps reduce these delays.
